prompt: A folder holds report.txt, report-v2.txt and report-FINAL.txt. What can it not tell you that a Git history can?

choices.text: Who changed what, when and why

choices.text: Whether the files can be opened
choices.why: Any editor answers that.

prompt: What does every commit after the first one point at?

choices.text: The next commit that will be made on it
choices.why: A commit cannot know its future; it points back.

choices.text: The commit before it, its parent
choices.why: Right. Each points at its parent, back to the first.

choices.text: The branch it was made on

prompt: What does a commit store?
hint: A photograph, not a list.

choices.why: That is what a diff shows, computed from two snapshots.

choices.text: A snapshot of every tracked file
choices.why: Right. Git shows differences by comparing two snapshots.

choices.text: A copy of the whole disk
choices.why: Only the files the repository tracks.

choices.text: The undo history kept by your text editor
choices.why: Git never sees the editor.

prompt: The shared server is lost. With Git, what survives?
hint: Where does the history live?

choices.why: Right. Every copy is a complete repository.

choices.text: Nothing; the server held the history
choices.why: That describes a centralised system, not Git.

prompt: Before the first commit, Git needs to know who you are: git config --global user.___ "Ana Souza"
hint: The other setting is user.email.

prompt: Which are the three places a change passes through in Git?

choices.text: A branch, a tag and a remote repository
choices.why: Those are names for commits, not stages.

prompt: Ana runs git add index.html, edits the file again, then commits. What goes into the commit?

choices.text: Nothing; the file changed after add

choices.text: The file as it was when she added it

choices.text: Both versions, as two separate commits in a row
choices.why: One commit, one snapshot.

choices.text: No; it needs git add first
choices.why: Right. It stays untracked.

choices.text: Yes, if the file is saved
choices.why: Saving does not make it tracked.

prompt: To stop tracking notes.txt but keep the file on disk: git rm ___ notes.txt

prompt: What does git mv menu.html cardapio.html do that a plain mv does not?

choices.text: It renames the file on the server

prompt: Ana staged index.html and wants to see exactly what the next commit will contain. Which command?

choices.why: The line is gone, so blame has nothing to show for it.

prompt: What does git log --oneline print for each commit?

choices.text: Its short id and the message's first line

choices.text: Every file it changed, and how many lines

prompt: What does git diff 4a1c2e3 6555c9b show?

prompt: Ana has broken index.html while editing and has not staged it. How does she get back the last committed version?

reset is local.

prompt: Match each reset mode to what it keeps.
hint: The branch moves in all three.

prompt: After a git reset --hard, a commit is missing from git log. Where can Ana still find its id?

prompt: What is a branch in Git?

choices.text: A folder copy of the files

choices.text: A name that points at one commit

prompt: What does HEAD normally name?

choices.text: The newest commit on the server

choices.text: The branch you are on now
choices.why: Right. A new commit moves that branch.

choices.text: The branch with the most commits

prompt: To create the branch sunday-hours and move onto it in one command: git switch ___ sunday-hours

prompt: git branch -d experiment refuses because the branch is not merged. What does that refusal protect?

choices.why: Right. They would be reachable only through the reflog.

choices.text: The files in the working tree

main is not the branch being deleted.

prompt: Ana has an uncommitted edit to index.html, and the other branch has a different index.html. What does git switch do?

switch does not merge.

prompt: When does a merge stop with a conflict?

choices.text: When both changed the same lines

prompt: Halfway through a ticket, you find nobody decided whether refunds are needed. What do you do?
hint: A day asking beats two days guessing.

choices.why: That may be work nobody wanted.

choices.text: Ask, and mark the card blocked
choices.why: Right. Write the question on the ticket.

choices.text: Leave refunds out and say nothing
choices.why: The gap then surfaces at the review.

choices.text: Move the ticket to done and open a new one
choices.why: It is not done.

prompt: git status --short shows ?? images/. What is true of that folder?
hint: Git has never been told about it.

choices.why: Ignored files are not listed at all.
Right. No commit will include it until git add.

choices.text: It has a merge conflict in it
choices.why: A conflict shows as UU.

choices.text: It was deleted in the last commit
choices.why: A deletion shows as D.

prompt: What is the quickest way to see what a colleague will get from your branch?
hint: A machine that is not yours.

choices.text: Open the files in your editor
choices.why: Your editor shows your disk, untracked files included.

choices.text: Clone it into a fresh folder
choices.why: Right. It holds only what was pushed.

choices.text: Run git log on your own laptop
choices.why: The log lists commits, not what they left out.
That moves the cost onto them.

prompt: Why does CI run the checks on a freshly created machine each time?
hint: Nothing of anybody's laptop is on it.

choices.text: Fresh machines are faster than laptops
choices.why: Speed is not the point.

choices.text: Because Git cannot run on a developer's laptop
choices.why: Git runs everywhere.
The results show on the pull request.

choices.text: So local-only files cannot hide a problem
choices.why: Right. It sees only what was pushed.

prompt: CI reads a check as passed when the script ends with exit status ___.
hint: Anything else is a failure.

prompt: Match each statement to what it belongs to.
hint: One applies to every ticket.

pairs.left: The menu shows gluten, milk and eggs
Reviewed, checks green, tested and released

prompt: A missing file can be caught at four points. Where is it cheapest?
hint: The lower on the ladder, the cheaper.

choices.text: git status on your own laptop
choices.why: Right. One command.

choices.text: In the reviewer's reading of the pull request
choices.why: Twenty minutes of somebody else's time.
An hour, and a round trip.

choices.text: On the live site, by a customer
choices.why: The most expensive rung: trust.

prompt: What is the daily stand-up for?
hint: Coordination, not reporting.

choices.text: Reporting each person's hours to a manager
choices.why: That turns it into a status report.
That is refinement.

choices.text: Solving every problem in detail together
choices.why: Problems are solved after, by those involved.
Right. Named there, solved after.

prompt: Walking the board at the stand-up, which column comes first?
hint: Nearest to finished.

choices.why: Starting is discussed last.
Right. What does each card need to move right?
Second, after review.
Done needs nothing, so it is skipped.

prompt: Why does planning leave slack below the team's capacity?
hint: Something always takes longer.

choices.text: So the team can leave early on Fridays
choices.why: The slack is for the unexpected, not time off.
The slack is not a correction of velocity.

choices.text: So the goal survives a normal week
choices.why: Right. Bugs, slow reviews, unready tickets.

choices.text: The product owner asks for it
choices.why: Developers decide how much fits.

prompt: Match each end-of-sprint meeting to what it looks at.
hint: One looks at the product, one at the team.

pairs.right: The finished work, with the people who asked

right_distractors: Each person's mistakes, one by one

prompt: A retrospective finds six problems. What makes it most likely something changes?
hint: Changes that happen beat changes that do not.

choices.why: Six at once usually means none happen.

choices.text: Writing the problems in a long document
choices.why: A list is not a change.
Right. And checked at the next retro.
Blame makes people stop saying what went wrong.

prompt: A problem raised at the stand-up and solved afterwards by the people involved goes to the parking ___.
hint: Where cars wait.

prompt: Who decides which of two tickets matters more?
hint: Developers supply the cost.

choices.why: Right. The team makes the cost honest.

choices.text: The developer who will build it
choices.why: They know the cost, not the priority.
Testing informs risk.

choices.text: The designer, since customers see the screens
choices.why: Design decides how it works, not what comes first.

prompt: A design shows only the case where everything works. What is most worth asking the designer?
hint: The cases the drawing does not show.

choices.text: Whether the colours could be brighter
choices.why: Taste, and not a missing case.

choices.text: Why the design took so long to arrive
choices.why: Not a question about the product.

choices.text: What the page says when it fails
choices.why: Right. Errors, empty states, long text.
The design is how the customer uses it.

prompt: When is a tester's view of how things fail most useful?
hint: Before or after the assumption is built?

choices.why: Then every finding is a delay.

choices.text: After customers have complained about it
choices.why: The most expensive moment.

choices.text: Never; CI replaces that job now
choices.why: CI sees what a script can see.
Right. In refinement a negative balance is one sentence.

prompt: Product, design, development and QA each finish and hand over, in turn. Where do the surprises tend to land?
hint: What each handover lost appears when the last person uses the result.

choices.why: Nothing has been handed over yet.
They accumulate towards the end.
Each handover loses something.

choices.text: At the end, all at once
choices.why: Right. Where they cost the most.

prompt: What most cheaply brings a misunderstanding forward?
hint: Is this what you meant?

choices.why: More hours on a misunderstanding build more of it.

choices.text: Writing a longer ticket after the review
choices.why: After the review is when the surprise already landed.

choices.text: Waiting for QA to find it at the end
choices.why: That puts the question at the end.
Right. A screenshot on day two.

prompt: Product asks for something that would take two sprints. Which reply helps most?
hint: Information, not a refusal.

choices.why: It can; the question is at what cost.

choices.text: Yes, I will fit it in somehow.
choices.why: It hides the trade-off and costs the team.
The cost is for developers to give.

choices.text: Two sprints; a smaller version takes three days.
choices.why: Right. A cost and an alternative, so product can decide.
